The test image shows a patch of dead/wilted soybean plants in the center of an otherwise healthy green field. The affected plants are completely dried, brown, and collapsed while surrounding plants remain healthy. This patch pattern of mature plant death is characteristic of root/stem diseases.

Top candidates: Phytophthora, Sudden_death_syndrome, Rhizoctonia, Pythium_damping_off

Let me view the Phytophthora reference image to confirm.

The Phytophthora reference image (top-left panel) shows a nearly identical pattern to the test image — a concentrated patch of completely dead, dried, wilted mature soybean plants with brown/tan stems in an otherwise green healthy field, with wet dark soil visible. This matches perfectly.

Key matching features:
- Patch of mature, completely dead/wilted plants in center of field
- Brown dried stems with dead foliage
- Surrounding plants remain healthy and green
- Dark/moist soil conditions visible (consistent with Phytophthora favoring wet conditions)
- Plants appear to have collapsed/wilted from root/stem rot
